2025-12 — [a national statistical release calendar for 2026 was issued expressly under section 27(1) of the Act](2025-12-01-zamstats-national-statistical-release-calendar-2026), operationalising its release-planning mandate.

2026-03-24 — [a new Statistician-General was appointed, the statutory chief executive under section 11](2026-03-24-zamstats-statistician-general-appointment).

Both are the statute working rather than changing, which is the more useful thing to record about a law eight years old: the offices it creates are filled and the duties it imposes are being discharged on schedule.

summary: The 2023 Act gained [its first implementing regulations](2025-08-29-zambia-access-to-information-general-regulations-2025) and then [commission guidelines translating its duties into operational guidance](2025-12-05-hrc-access-to-information-guidelines-2025).
developments:
[Act No. 24 of 2023 came into force on 25 June 2024, granting a citizen or residence-permit holder the right to access information held by an information holder](2023-12-26-zambia-access-to-information-act-2023).

2025-08-29 — [Statutory Instrument No. 56 of 2025 supplied the request forms, fees and procedures needed to make the right operative](2025-08-29-zambia-access-to-information-general-regulations-2025) — the step without which an access statute is unusable.

2025-12-05 — [the rights commission issued guidelines as Government Notice No. 1624 of 2025, translating the Act's duties into operational guidance](2025-12-05-hrc-access-to-information-guidelines-2025).

Two years from enactment to a usable procedure is the shape of it. No count of requests made, granted or refused under the Act is published.

summary: The Commissioner [names registration as the first step and weak internal systems and limited awareness as continuing gaps](2026-06-07-lusaka-star-data-protection-act-enforcement-hurdles).
developments:
[Act No. 3 of 2021 establishes the Office of the Data Protection Commissioner and, at sections 70 and 71, the cross-border transfer regime](2021-03-24-zambia-data-protection-act-2021).

2026-06 — [the Data Protection Commissioner went on record identifying registration of controllers as the necessary first step, and naming weak internal systems and limited awareness as continuing implementation gaps](2026-06-07-lusaka-star-data-protection-act-enforcement-hurdles).

A regulator publicly naming its own enforcement obstacles is a more useful record than a compliance statistic, and it is the only one available: no registration count, no enforcement notice and no penalty under the Act is held, five years after it was passed.

summary: The continental convention on cyber security and personal data protection [is signed, ratified and deposited](2024-07-08-au-convention-cyber-security-personal-data-protection-ratification-status).
developments:
[The African Union's own treaty status table records signature on 29 January 2016, ratification on 15 December 2020 and deposit on 24 March 2021](2024-07-08-au-convention-cyber-security-personal-data-protection-ratification-status) of the convention on cyber security and personal data protection.

It is the clearest binding regional legal-harmonisation instrument the country has joined, and the base holds nothing downstream of it: no domestic measure attributed to the convention, no report under it, and no regional body's assessment of Zambian compliance. Ratification is where this record stops.

summary: A statutory transfer regime sits at [sections 70 and 71 of the data protection statute](2021-03-24-zambia-data-protection-act-2021); no authorisation or enforcement under it is held.
developments:
[The Data Protection Act, 2021 carries the cross-border data transfer regime at sections 70 and 71](2021-03-24-zambia-data-protection-act-2021).

That is the instrument. What the base does not hold is any evidence of it operating: no adequacy determination for another country, no transfer authorisation granted, no condition imposed and no enforcement action. A transfer regime that has produced no visible decision in five years tells a reader about capacity rather than about policy — and the Commissioner's own account of registration as the outstanding first step is the corroboration.

summary: The standards bureau [states more than 50 international standards adopted within a catalogue of over 6,500](2026-08-29-zabs-standards-development), and an extractives validation [scored 81 points](2026-06-26-zambia-2026-eiti-validation-report).
developments:
[The standards bureau states that more than 50 international standards have been adopted as Zambian Standards, within a catalogue of more than 6,500 national standards across sectors including information and communication technology](2026-08-29-zabs-standards-development). The page is undated, so the figures are dated to retrieval.

2026-06-25 — [the extractives transparency board found the country's fourth validation under the 2023 standard achieved a very good overall score of 81 points](2026-06-26-zambia-2026-eiti-validation-report), an international standard applied and independently assessed here rather than merely adopted.

Adoption counts and an assessed score are different kinds of evidence; the second is the rarer and it is not about digital.

summary: A constitutional consultation [reported more than 11,864 public submissions](2025-11-25-technical-committee-constitutional-amendment-report), and a bill [was deferred after civil-society concerns](2025-08-21-government-defers-ngo-bill-wider-consultations).
developments:
[A statute places non-state representation on national, provincial and district development coordinating committees and cluster advisory groups, and provides for state and non-state submission of budget policy proposals](2020-10-23-national-planning-and-budgeting-act-2020-zambia) — participation as a standing statutory arrangement rather than an event.

2025-08 — [the responsible minister deferred a bill on non-governmental organisations after civil-society and non-governmental stakeholders raised concerns](2025-08-21-government-defers-ngo-bill-wider-consultations), an explicit government response to non-state input.

2025-11-25 — [a nationwide constitutional consultation reporting more than 11,864 public submissions through public sittings, submission boxes, website and email was handed to the President](2025-11-25-technical-committee-constitutional-amendment-report). It is the largest documented consultation on this ledger and its subject is the constitution rather than digital policy.

summary: The regulator's [2025 sector report carries its own subscription and affordability figures](2026-03-28-zicta-2025-ict-postal-sector-market-performance-report-zambia-monitor), and the [mobile money levy schedule was revised](2025-12-30-mobile-money-transaction-levy-amendment-act-2025).
developments:
[An external country diagnostic published Zambia-specific prepaid one-gigabyte and voice basket prices](2023-08-02-zambia-digital-ecosystem-country-assessment-mAccess-diagnostic-digital-development) — the base's earlier affordability position, from a foreign tool rather than a domestic series.

2026-03 — [the regulator's 2025 ICT and postal sector market performance report gave its own current mobile subscription and affordability figures](2026-03-28-zicta-2025-ict-postal-sector-market-performance-report-zambia-monitor), which is the more durable source.

2025-12-30 — [an Act revised the person-to-person mobile money transfer levy schedule, effective 1 January 2026](2025-12-30-mobile-money-transaction-levy-amendment-act-2025). A transfer levy is an affordability question for the poorest users of the payment system, and no assessment of its incidence accompanies it.

summary: A [memorandum to co-invest in a national artificial-intelligence data centre](2026-05-26-zambia-huawei-national-ai-data-centre-mou-ovp), and a [national operator partnering on next-generation cloud](2026-07-17-paratus-zambia-zadara-cloud-platform-techtrends).
developments:
[A parliamentary committee report on ICT infrastructure is the base's standing account of national data-centre capacity](2023-01-01-zambia-ict-infrastructure-vis-a-vis-fintech-growth-national-assembly).

2026-05-26 — [the state technology institute and a vendor signed a memorandum to co-invest in a national artificial-intelligence data centre](2026-05-26-zambia-huawei-national-ai-data-centre-mou-ovp), announced at a mobile congress.

2026-07 — [a national operator partnered with a cloud provider to deliver next-generation cloud services](2026-07-17-paratus-zambia-zadara-cloud-platform-techtrends). Two commitments and no capacity figure: neither states megawatts, racks, tier or a commissioning date, so the base can record that capacity is being contracted for and not how much.

summary: A [procurement notice for servers and a backup platform](2025-08-13-onap-backup-solution-national-coordinating-office-nao) and a [national operator cloud partnership](2026-07-17-paratus-zambia-zadara-cloud-platform-techtrends), over a committee finding on disaster-recovery sites.
developments:
[A parliamentary committee review of the state technology institute carries the base's finding on disaster-recovery sites](2023-01-01-review-of-operations-and-management-of-smart-zambia-national-assembly), alongside the government wide area network rollout.

2025-08 — [a national coordinating office issued a procurement notice for servers and an open network automation platform backup solution](2025-08-13-onap-backup-solution-national-coordinating-office-nao).

2026-07 — [a national operator partnered to deliver cloud services](2026-07-17-paratus-zambia-zadara-cloud-platform-techtrends) that would carry backup capacity commercially.

One agency's procurement and one commercial partnership is what the window holds. No government-wide backup policy, recovery-point objective or tested restoration is on the record.

summary: Construction launched on a [250MW solar plant with 600MWh of storage](2026-04-21-leopards-hill-250mw-solar-battery-plant-zanis), and a [500MW solar power purchase agreement was signed](2026-06-19-zesco-ks-eco-solutions-500mw-solar-pact-linkedin).
developments:
[A parliamentary committee report on ICT infrastructure sets out the energy constraint on data centres](2023-01-01-zambia-ict-infrastructure-vis-a-vis-fintech-growth-national-assembly) — the base's standing position on the supply side.

2026-04-21 — [construction was launched on a 250MW solar plant with 150MW and 600MWh of battery storage, aimed at stabilising national supply](2026-04-21-leopards-hill-250mw-solar-battery-plant-zanis).

2026-06 — [the national utility signed a 500MW solar power purchase agreement with battery storage](2026-06-19-zesco-ks-eco-solutions-500mw-solar-pact-linkedin).

Both are generation rather than a data-centre power arrangement, and neither states a connection date or a firm capacity for digital load. Nothing at all in the base addresses water for cooling.

summary: A [grid project brought power for the first time to a catchment of 42,000](2025-08-25-mitete-connects-to-grid-rea), and a [US$200 million access programme launched](2025-12-10-zambia-launches-ascent-200-million-electricity-access-rea).
developments:
[The Rural Electrification Act, 2023 continues the rural electrification authority and its fund, repealing the 2003 Act](2023-04-18-rural-electrification-act-2023).

2025-08 — [the authority completed a grid development project in Western Province, bringing grid power for the first time to a catchment population of 42,000](2025-08-25-mitete-connects-to-grid-rea). A named completed connection with a population behind it is the rarest form of evidence on this indicator.

2025-12 — [a US$200 million programme was launched targeting universal electricity access by 2030](2025-12-10-zambia-launches-ascent-200-million-electricity-access-rea). The gap between one district connected and universal access by 2030 is the whole of what this row cannot yet measure: no national access rate or connection series is held.

summary: An input voucher [ran electronic know-your-customer across all 116 districts, removing 225,016 ineligible beneficiaries](2026-01-28-zambia-fisp-e-voucher-pdu).
developments:
[The Electronic Government Act, 2021 requires public bodies to offer electronic proof of identity issued under the National Registration Act and to enable joint automated procedures and data sharing between public bodies](2021-05-19-zambia-electronic-government-act-2021-batch4_dpi_a) — the legal basis.

2026-01 — [the farmer input support voucher reached all 116 districts using electronic know-your-customer verification cross-checked against the pension authority and other registers, removing 212,851 and then a further 12,165 ineligible beneficiaries](2026-01-28-zambia-fisp-e-voucher-pdu). That is identity being queried against other registers across the whole country, which is what this indicator asks and what most of the continent cannot show.

2025-09-29 — [a digital identity cooperation agreement with Ethiopia was formalised, use-case driven and explicitly linking identity verification to civil registration, social protection and mobile money](2025-10-30-zambia-ethiopia-digital-id-cooperation-wb-blog).

summary: The health ministry [published a national HL7 FHIR implementation guide defining profiles across five named systems](2025-11-21-zambia-zm-core-fhir-implementation-guide).
developments:
[The health ministry published its own national HL7 FHIR R5 interoperability specification, defining reusable profiles for exchanging data among the clinical system, the health management information system, the master facility list, the electronic logistics system and the human resources information system](2025-11-21-zambia-zm-core-fhir-implementation-guide), superseding the earlier strategy's draft framework.

A published implementation guide naming the systems it connects is a stronger artefact than an interoperability policy, and it is unusual: most of the continent's health interoperability positions on this frame are workshops. What is not yet held is any statement of conformance — no system is recorded as implementing the guide.

summary: Higher education institutions [were directed to submit student data for a centralised database with institution-independent index numbers](2026-03-25-zambia-hea-student-indexing-reform).
developments:
[A mid-term review records education management information system reform under way with a teacher database review under consideration](2024-12-13-zambia-zeep-mid-term-review-aide-memoire).

2026-03 — [the higher education authority directed all institutions to submit student data for a centralised national student database with institution-independent index numbers](2026-03-25-zambia-hea-student-indexing-reform), under the 2021 amendment Act. No linkage to the national identity or civil registration registers is stated, which is the connection that would make the index durable.

2026-06-12 — [a sector-wide education and skills data challenge and its technical working group were launched](2026-06-12-adea-education-and-skills-data-challenge-esdc-initiative-zambia), the leading sector data-governance development in the window.

summary: A workshop [brought five agencies and line ministries together and produced a draft roadmap and technical committee](2025-11-17-zambia-ilo-digital-convergence-roadmap).
developments:
2025-09 — [a US$100 million digital acceleration programme was approved, its interoperable and secure platforms pillar funding digital government services and data exchange](2025-09-23-zambia-dzap-world-bank-press-release).

2025-09-14 to 21 — [a workshop in Kitwe brought the pension authority, the health insurance authority, the workers' compensation board, the disability agency, the state technology institute and line ministries together, producing a draft convergence roadmap and a technical committee to link the social protection systems](2025-11-17-zambia-ilo-digital-convergence-roadmap).

Naming the five bodies that have to connect is the useful part. A roadmap and a committee are not an exchange: no interface, data-sharing agreement or go-live date follows from either in the record.

summary: The registration department [began computerising card, passport and citizenship-document issuance](2025-08-29-zambia-monitor-digitalisation-identity-services), financed through a [US$100 million programme](2025-09-23-zambia-dzap-world-bank-press-release).
developments:
2025-08 — [the home affairs permanent secretary announced that the registration department has begun computerising national registration card, passport and citizenship-document issuance in collaboration with the state technology institute, targeting online applications including from the diaspora](2025-08-29-zambia-monitor-digitalisation-identity-services).

2025-09 — [a US$100 million digital acceleration programme was approved, the financing vehicle for the new identity and civil registration system](2025-09-23-zambia-dzap-world-bank-press-release).

What the base cannot yet say is who will run it. Both accounts describe a build financed externally and integrated by a vendor to be selected; no statement of in-house operating capacity, staffing or vendor exit arrangement is held.

summary: A national authentication service [runs single sign-on, OpenID Connect, multi-factor and passwordless credentials for e-government](2026-08-29-zambia-zampass-about).
developments:
[The state technology institute publishes the service description of the national authentication and access-control service: single sign-on, OpenID Connect, multi-factor authentication and passwordless credentials for electronic government services](2026-08-29-zambia-zampass-about).

An operating authentication service with named protocols is the strongest identity artefact on this ledger, and it is what makes the downstream uses recorded elsewhere possible. The page is undated, so the position is dated to retrieval, and no user count, uptime figure or list of relying services is published — so the base can describe the service and not its reach.

summary: Civil registration funding [was raised 67 per cent after advocacy](2026-05-21-zambia-ghai-crvs-budget-case-study), against only 22 per cent of under-fives with registered births.
developments:
[The Births and Deaths Registration Act of 1973 requires uniform registration of every birth and death](1973-03-23-zambia-births-and-deaths-registration-act), the statutory root from which a birth-time identity number would derive.

2026-05 — [advocacy reversed a proposed cut and secured a 67 per cent funding increase for civil registration in the 2026 budget, and helped establish a 26-member parliamentary caucus in October 2025, explicitly framed as the foundation the digital identity reform needs, since only 22 per cent of under-fives have registered births and 15 per cent in rural areas](2026-05-21-zambia-ghai-crvs-budget-case-study).

Those two percentages are the finding. An identity number issued at birth reaches roughly a fifth of children, and a budget increase is the first movement toward changing that.

summary: A [system integrator was invited to deploy and integrate foundational identity and civil registration modules](2025-09-09-zambia-dzap-early-market-engagement), over a [regulation deriving the card number from the birth record](2019-01-01-zambia-national-registration-regulations-2019).
developments:
[Regulation 6(2)(a) of the National Registration Regulations, 2019 is the clearest legal linkage: for a person born in Zambia the national registration card number is derived from that person's birth-registration record](2019-01-01-zambia-national-registration-regulations-2019). The link exists in law.

2025-09 — [the acceleration project invited vendors for a system integrator to deploy, customise and integrate foundational digital identity and civil registration core modules, including data migration and enrolment kits](2025-09-09-zambia-dzap-early-market-engagement) — the procurement that would make the legal link technical.

2026-04 — [the country's civil registration experience informed validation of a continental interoperability framework's non-functional requirements](2026-04-27-zambia-apai-crvs-acsa-workshop); it is not among the six pilot countries.

summary: Passport and travel-document applications [now require a national authentication account on the government service bus](2025-12-11-zambia-znbc-online-passport-launch).
developments:
[The Electronic Government Act, 2021 creates a citizen card as the cross-system identity and authentication credential](2021-05-19-zambia-electronic-government-act-2021-batch4_dpi_a).

2025-12 — [the home affairs minister announced that passport, diplomatic passport, refugee travel document and identity travel document applications are integrated into the government service bus and require a national authentication account](2025-12-11-zambia-znbc-online-passport-launch) — the clearest live downstream use of the authentication service by another government system.

2026-01 — [an agricultural input voucher ran electronic know-your-customer across all 116 districts](2026-01-28-zambia-fisp-e-voucher-pdu), the largest-scale consumption of identity the base holds for the country.

summary: A [2025 Act mandates an electronic single window and single payment point for trade duties](2025-08-08-the-border-management-and-trade-facilitation-act-2025); a [new payment Act is passed but not commenced](2026-04-08-national-payment-system-act-2026).
developments:
2025-08 — [the border management and trade facilitation statute mandates an electronic single window and a single payment point platform for import, export and transit duties, taxes, fees and levies](2025-08-08-the-border-management-and-trade-facilitation-act-2025) — a direct business-to-government payment integration for traders.

2026-04-08 — [a new National Payment System Act replaces the 2007 statute, creating licensing and market-conduct rules for payment service providers covering these rails](2026-04-08-national-payment-system-act-2026). It is not yet commenced, which is the operative fact: the regime that would govern these payments is enacted and not in force.

No transaction volume or value on either rail is published.

summary: Mobile wallets [reached a bank's point-of-sale terminals and cash machines](2026-03-04-momo-payments-on-zanaco-pos-launch), and [councils were onboarded for electronic fee payment](2026-07-10-e-council-services-enhance-efficiency-at-solwezi-municipal-council).
developments:
[The National Payment Systems Act of 2007 established regulatory authority over the payment mechanisms underlying these rails](2007-04-12-national-payment-systems-act).

2026-03 — [a mobile money wallet gained interoperability with a commercial bank's point-of-sale terminals and cash machines](2026-03-04-momo-payments-on-zanaco-pos-launch), a concrete person-to-business and cash-out expansion.

2026-07 — [local authorities including one municipal council were onboarded to the government service bus, enabling electronic payment of council fees and levies](2026-07-10-e-council-services-enhance-efficiency-at-solwezi-municipal-council). Person-to-government payment reaching local rather than central government is the newer half, and no count of councils, transactions or value is published against it.

summary: The [2026 payment Act carries a dedicated consumer-protection regime](2026-04-08-national-payment-system-act-2026), over a [2018 directive prohibiting 26 categories of charge](2018-09-04-boz-notice-prohibition-of-unwarranted-charges-and-fees-directives-2018).
developments:
[A central bank directive prohibits 26 categories of unwarranted charges and fees on financial services](2018-09-04-boz-notice-prohibition-of-unwarranted-charges-and-fees-directives-2018) — the clearest standalone consumer-protection instrument for digital and card payments, and eight years old.

2026-03 — [the central bank's journal carried a notice on registration of virtual asset service providers](2026-03-01-zambanker-march-2026-edition), moving crypto activity toward supervised status.

2026-04-08 — [the new payment system Act carries a dedicated consumer-protection regime alongside market-conduct rules for payment service providers](2026-04-08-national-payment-system-act-2026). It is not yet commenced. No complaint volume, redress statistic or enforcement action under the 2018 directive is held, so what protection currently delivers cannot be read.

summary: A [sample based registration system was launched to capture deaths occurring outside health facilities](2026-05-07-zambia-launches-srs-vs-silent-deaths).
developments:
2026-05 — [the health ministry launched a sample based registration system with vital statistics, extending continuous civil-registration coverage to deaths outside health facilities](2026-05-07-zambia-launches-srs-vs-silent-deaths) — what the reporting describes as the silent deaths the register was missing.

Deaths outside facilities are the harder half of civil registration everywhere, and a sample-based system is an acknowledgement that universal capture is not close. No coverage estimate, sample size or first result is published, and the base holds no statement of the population register's own completeness to read it against.

summary: A [national spatial data infrastructure policy and geoportal launched](2026-06-16-znsdi-policy-and-zambia-portal-launched), over a [2017 regulation assigning the postcode and address database](2017-01-09-zambia-postal-services-postcode-regulations-2017).
developments:
[A 2017 regulation under the postal services statute assigns the communications authority responsibility to regulate, allocate and manage postcodes and to maintain a national address database, and sets the technical postcode model](2017-01-09-zambia-postal-services-postcode-regulations-2017). The legal duty has existed for nine years.

2026-06-16 — [a national spatial data infrastructure policy and a national geoportal were launched, which government describes as ending fragmentation of address and geospatial data across agencies](2026-06-16-znsdi-policy-and-zambia-portal-launched).

A geoportal is not an address register, and the record does not say whether the postcode database the 2017 regulation requires was ever built — which is the question the launch implicitly answers by describing fragmentation.

summary: The final register [was certified at 8,786,300 voters with polling-station detail across 13,529 stations](2026-05-08-ecz-registered-voters-per-polling-station-2026), after [1,615,922 were added](2026-03-06-zambia-mass-voter-registration-ministerial-statement).
developments:
2026-03-06 — [a ministerial statement reported a 48-day mass registration exercise that added 1,615,922 new voters, bringing the provisional register to 8,861,918, followed by inspection and biometric verification](2026-03-06-zambia-mass-voter-registration-ministerial-statement).

2026-05-02 — [the commission announced certification of the register for the general election on 4 May](2026-05-02-ecz-certification-of-register-of-voters).

2026-05-08 — [the final register was published at 8,786,300 registered voters with polling-station-level detail across 13,529 polling stations](2026-05-08-ecz-registered-voters-per-polling-station-2026). The difference between the provisional register and the certified one is what inspection and biometric verification removed, and neither account explains it — which for an electoral register is the thing a reader most wants explained.

progress: Mixed, the register grew while active accounts barely moved
summary: Register holders [rose to 6,571,699 while active tax accounts rose only from 379,985 to 388,779](2026-07-29-zambia-tpin-holders-active-tax-accounts).
developments:
[A 2023 amendment made obtaining a taxpayer identification number a statutory obligation, effective 1 January 2024](2023-12-22-zambia-income-tax-amendment-act-2023).

2026-07 — [the revenue authority's annual report shows register holders growing from 6,015,533 in 2024 to 6,571,699 in 2025, while active tax accounts rose only from 379,985 to 388,779](2026-07-29-zambia-tpin-holders-active-tax-accounts). Six per cent of the register is active. A statutory registration obligation produces a register, and this is what a register produced that way looks like.

2025-10 — [an amendment bill enabling information exchange among revenue authority divisions and with the entities it establishes was tabled, commencing 1 January 2026](2025-10-29-zambia-revenue-authority-amendment-bill-2025), which is the reform aimed at the gap.

summary: A national social registry [is Cabinet-approved and still under design](2025-11-10-zambia-gewel2-additional-financing-project-paper), while the ministry [launched a digital strategy and continuity guidelines](2025-11-13-zambias-community-development-ministry-unveils-three-digital-strategies).
developments:
[A project appraisal gives the fullest account of the beneficiary system's architecture, coverage and function](2022-06-14-zambia-scaling-up-shock-responsive-social-protection-project-pad5062) — the operational system carrying the social cash transfer.

2025-11 — [a project paper records the current standing: the beneficiary system operational, and a dynamic national social registry approved by Cabinet in April 2025 with its concept note endorsed in September, still under design](2025-11-10-zambia-gewel2-additional-financing-project-paper).

2025-11-13 — [the responsible ministry launched a ministerial digital strategy, business continuity and disaster recovery guidelines and ICT security guidelines](2025-11-13-zambias-community-development-ministry-unveils-three-digital-strategies) underpinning the existing system and its planned registry expansion. Continuity guidelines before a registry is built is the right order and an unusual one.

summary: Electronic invoicing moved into court enforcement: [seven taxpayers prosecuted against more than 44,000 businesses registered](2026-05-11-7-taxpayes-to-face-court-over-failure-to-use-smart-invoice-zra).
developments:
[A 2023 amendment defined the electronic invoicing system in law, effective 1 January 2024](2023-12-22-the-value-added-tax-amendment-act-2023).

2025-08 — [a sectoral mandate onboarded 494 filling stations, 59 of them by direct system integration](2025-08-06-zra-intensifies-national-campaign-smart-invoicing-filling-stations) — integration rather than issuance being the harder half.

2026-05-11 — [the revenue authority moved non-compliance into court against seven taxpayers, with more than 44,000 businesses registered](2026-05-11-7-taxpayes-to-face-court-over-failure-to-use-smart-invoice-zra). A system passes from onboarding into enforcement exactly once, and this is that point; seven prosecutions against a register of that size is a signal rather than a campaign, and no compliance rate is published to read it against.

progress: No change, one outage and no description of the system
summary: The land system's electronic services [were temporarily disrupted, explained to Parliament in a ministerial statement](2025-03-27-ministerial-statement-temporary-disruption-zilas).
developments:
[A ministerial statement to the National Assembly addressed a temporary disruption of the ministry's electronic services on the government service bus through the land administration system](2025-03-27-ministerial-statement-temporary-disruption-zilas).

That is the base's only record of the country's land administration system, and it is an outage rather than a description. No coverage figure, parcel count, restoration date or account of what the system does is held — so what can be stated is that a land information system exists, is connected to the government service bus, and stopped working for long enough to require a statement to Parliament.

summary: [2,000 devices were handed over for all 116 local authorities](2025-09-04-smart-zambia-2000-ict-devices-local-government-techafricanews) and [eight were onboarded to the government service bus](2026-07-02-eight-local-authorities-go-digital-mlgrd).
developments:
[The 2026 budget address carries the connectivity and electronic government commitments for local government](2025-09-26-2026-budget-address-gwan-local-authorities).

2025-09 — [the state technology institute handed 1,780 laptops and 220 desktops to the local government ministry for distribution to all 116 local authorities plus district and provincial offices](2025-09-04-smart-zambia-2000-ict-devices-local-government-techafricanews).

2026-07 — [eight local authorities were onboarded to the government service bus](2026-07-02-eight-local-authorities-go-digital-mlgrd). Eight of 116 is the number worth keeping: equipment reached every authority and the platform reached seven per cent of them, which is the difference between hardware and a service.

summary: A target of [2,500 additional schools connected by end-2026](2026-04-16-2500-additional-schools-internet-connectivity-zanis), against one [completed rural school connection](2026-08-06-paratus-mphande-hills-primary-school-connectivity).
developments:
[The auditor general found the education ministry's electronic census software set aside as non-functional and replaced by an in-house spreadsheet tool](2024-01-01-oag-simplified-report-2023-accounts-e-census-wasteful-expenditure) — the base's standing finding on data capture in schools, and a costly one.

2026-04 — [the education ministry set a target of 2,500 additional schools connected to reliable internet by the end of 2026, prioritising rural and hard-to-reach areas](2026-04-16-2500-additional-schools-internet-connectivity-zanis). It is a target, not a rollout.

2026-08-06 — [an operator connected a rural primary school's computer laboratory by satellite](2026-08-06-paratus-mphande-hills-primary-school-connectivity). One completed deployment against that target, with four months to run and no progress count published.

summary: A [funding line for the integrated registration system](2025-09-26-2026-budget-address-gwan-local-authorities) sits behind [computerisation of card, passport and citizenship issuance](2025-08-29-zambia-monitor-digitalisation-identity-services).
developments:
2025-08 — [the registration department began computerising national registration card, passport and citizenship-document issuance with the state technology institute, targeting online applications including from the diaspora](2025-08-29-zambia-monitor-digitalisation-identity-services).

2025-09 — [the 2026 budget address carries a funding line for the integrated national registration information system](2025-09-26-2026-budget-address-gwan-local-authorities).

Both describe the centre. Neither states how many district or rural registry offices have been reached, what equipment they hold, or whether a citizen away from a provincial capital can transact — which is the whole of what this indicator asks, and the record does not answer it.

summary: A clinical system [consolidated 12 million patient records across 2,000+ facilities as an artificial-intelligence foundation](2026-04-15-zambia-smartcare-pro-ai-ready-healthcare).
developments:
2024-04 — [the agricultural research institute launched an application using artificial intelligence to diagnose and forecast crop pests and diseases for smallholder farmers](2024-04-16-zari-plantvillage-ai-app-launch) — the base's first operational deployment inside a Zambian sectoral system.

2026-03 — [the technology ministry signed a memorandum for an adaptive-learning pilot in secondary schools and vocational institutions](2026-03-09-mutati-launches-ai-pilot-in-education).

2026-04 — [a clinical system consolidated 12 million patient records across more than 2,000 facilities, framed by the state technology institute as the data foundation for artificial intelligence in the health management information system](2026-04-15-zambia-smartcare-pro-ai-ready-healthcare). The record layer arriving before the models is the right order, and it is the largest health dataset the base holds for the country.

summary: Draft [national ICT standards for the education sector were validated with a school hub installed](2026-07-01-unesco-zambia-ict-standards-education); [927 teachers have completed integration training](2026-06-12-itsa-chikuni-girls-teacher-ict-training).
developments:
[The ministry computer science syllabus for secondary forms one to four is the instrument establishing digital training in secondary education](2024-01-01-zambia-computer-science-secondary-syllabi-form-1-4).

2026-06 — [55 further teachers completed five-day ICT teaching-integration training at one secondary school, 927 cumulatively](2026-06-12-itsa-chikuni-girls-teacher-ict-training), reported by the implementing trust.

2026-07 — [draft national ICT standards and guidelines for the education sector were validated and a school ICT hub installed](2026-07-01-unesco-zambia-ict-standards-education). Standards and a cumulative teacher count are the two halves this indicator wants; what is missing between them is any national figure for how many of the country's secondary teachers can teach the syllabus.

summary: Accreditation [went to pilot on a quality-assurance system](2026-06-02-hea-qamis-online-accreditation-pilot), and a university [signed to host a continental-first artificial-intelligence institute](2026-06-09-mulungushi-university-ai-confucius-institute).
developments:
[The Zambia Qualifications Authority Act, 2024 continues the authority and establishes the national qualifications framework with a higher education sub-framework that registers, verifies and evaluates university qualifications](2024-08-16-zambia-qualifications-authority-act-2024).

2026-06-02 — [the higher education authority put its quality assurance management information system into pilot, digitising accreditation applications, after training 50 institutions' quality assurance and IT staff in March](2026-06-02-hea-qamis-online-accreditation-pilot).

2026-06-09 — [a university signed an agreement in Beijing to host the continent's first artificial-intelligence institute of its kind](2026-06-09-mulungushi-university-ai-confucius-institute). A facility and a qualification system moving in the same month; no enrolment, accreditation throughput or graduate figure accompanies either.

summary: Health charters [linked facility accountability to the citizen support portal](2025-11-27-national-health-service-delivery-charters), and [labour cases now reach districts with no office through it](2026-08-24-govt-pushes-digitalisation-to-expand-services).
developments:
2025-01 — [cabinet office launched the national citizen support portal](2025-01-28-government-launches-citizen-support-portal).

2025-11 — [national health service delivery charters formally linked facility-level accountability to the portal and to the anti-corruption commission's whistleblower system](2025-11-27-national-health-service-delivery-charters) — a feedback channel gaining a service standard to be measured against, which is what turns a complaint box into accountability.

2026-08 — [labour ministry staff were trained to handle labour cases through the portal, extending it to districts with no physical office](2026-08-24-govt-pushes-digitalisation-to-expand-services). No case volume, resolution rate or response time for the portal is published, so its reach can be described and its performance cannot.

summary: [More than 11,860 citizen submissions were handed to the President](2025-12-02-tcca-hands-over-report-to-president) and became [an enacted constitutional amendment](2025-12-18-constitution-of-zambia-amendment-act-2025).
developments:
[The 2016 constitutional amendment provides for citizen petition and public involvement in the legislative process](2016-01-05-constitution-of-zambia-amendment-act-2016).

2025-12-02 — [more than 11,860 citizen submissions to the constitutional reform process were formally handed to the President](2025-12-02-tcca-hands-over-report-to-president), converting a nationwide consultation into a policymaking input.

2025-12-18 — [a constitutional amendment was enacted creating a mixed-member proportional representation system with reserved National Assembly and council seats for women, youths and persons with disabilities](2025-12-18-constitution-of-zambia-amendment-act-2025). Consultation reaching enactment inside a month is the rarest sequence on this frame; what is not published is which of the submissions the amendment reflects.

summary: A constitutional amendment [reserved National Assembly and council seats for women](2025-12-18-constitution-of-zambia-amendment-act-2025), over a [cross-sector gender status report](2025-08-01-gender-status-report-2020-2024).
developments:
[The fifth cross-sector gender status report covers governance, poverty, education, health, employment, land and gender-based violence](2025-08-01-gender-status-report-2020-2024) — the standing official measurement.

2025-12-18 — [a constitutional amendment created a mixed-member proportional system with reserved National Assembly and council seats for women](2025-12-18-constitution-of-zambia-amendment-act-2025), the most consequential equity instrument on this ledger and one whose effect is testable at the next election.

2026-04 — [specified sexual offences were made non-bailable](2026-04-08-criminal-procedure-code-amendment-act-2026). What the base does not hold is any sex-disaggregated measure of digital access — of device ownership, internet use or digital skills — so gender equity here is read through representation and law rather than through technology.

summary: A [national policy replaced the 2015 one](2025-05-28-national-policy-on-persons-with-disabilities) and a constitutional amendment [reserved seats for persons with disabilities](2025-12-18-constitution-of-zambia-amendment-act-2025).
developments:
2025-05 — [a national policy on persons with disabilities replaced the 2015 policy](2025-05-28-national-policy-on-persons-with-disabilities).

2025-08 — [a disability inclusive service site assessment tool was validated with the health ministry and partners](2025-08-06-healthcare-access-for-persons-with-disabilities-assessment-tool), a measurement instrument rather than a statement of intent.

2025-12 — [a constitutional amendment reserved National Assembly and council seats for persons with disabilities](2025-12-18-constitution-of-zambia-amendment-act-2025).

Policy, a measuring tool and reserved representation in seven months is real movement. Nothing in the base addresses digital accessibility specifically: no website standard, no assistive-technology provision figure and no disaggregated access measure is held.

summary: A [national data science training hub launched](2025-09-16-zamstats-launches-national-data-science-hub) and a donor-funded nutrition platform [moved into government structures](2026-04-18-nipn-holds-legacy-event).
developments:
[The second national strategy for the development of statistics runs 2023-2027, grounded in the Statistics Act](2023-07-01-second-national-strategy-for-development-of-statistics-2023-2027).

2025-09 — [the statistics agency launched a national data science training hub, explicitly aligned to the Act and the eighth national development plan, with bilateral support](2025-09-16-zamstats-launches-national-data-science-hub).

2026-04 — [a donor-supported national information platform for nutrition transitioned from funded pilot into sustainable government structures](2026-04-18-nipn-holds-legacy-event). A pilot surviving the end of its funding is the test most such platforms fail, and it is the clearest evidence the strategy is producing durable capacity rather than projects.

summary: Digitising death notification [raised completeness from 11.9 to 17.4 per cent and cut reporting time from six days to three](2025-09-12-role-of-digital-systems-in-improving-death-reporting).
developments:
[The Statistics Act, 2018 establishes the agency and the national statistical system](2018-12-26-zambia-statistics-act-2018), the framework administrative statistics are produced under.

2025-09 — [a Zambia case study digitising the death-notification form raised completeness from 11.9 to 17.4 per cent and cut reporting time from six days to three](2025-09-12-role-of-digital-systems-in-improving-death-reporting). Both figures matter and the first is the sobering one: after digitisation, fewer than one death in five is captured.

2026-04 — [a multisectoral nutrition information platform integrating administrative data moved into government structures](2026-04-18-nipn-holds-legacy-event), an example of the same chain working across sectors rather than within one.

summary: Four satellite rainfall products [were evaluated against 34 national stations](2026-07-31-evaluating-satellite-rainfall-products-against-ground-based-observations-zambia), and [21 surface stations are being upgraded](2026-05-26-zambia-wfp-uk-met-office-launch-usd-3-6-million-initiative).
developments:
[A peer-review assessment of the meteorological department confirms operational use of geostationary satellite imagery](2024-04-02-country-hydromet-diagnostics-zambia-nmhs-peer-review-report) — the baseline position.

2026-05-26 — [a US$3.6 million initiative was launched to upgrade 21 surface stations and install four upper-air stations, closing data gaps that limit forecast and satellite-product accuracy](2026-05-26-zambia-wfp-uk-met-office-launch-usd-3-6-million-initiative). Ground stations are what satellite products are calibrated against, so this is the unglamorous half of satellite capability.

2026-07 — [a peer-reviewed study evaluated four satellite rainfall products against 34 national stations and made operational recommendations](2026-07-31-evaluating-satellite-rainfall-products-against-ground-based-observations-zambia). Independent evaluation of the products actually in use is rarer than the use itself.

summary: [Over EUR 200 million in Team Europe investments](2025-11-12-commissioner-sikela-announces-team-europe-investments) and a [2026 partnership dialogue](2026-02-26-team-europe-and-zambia-discuss-reforms-and-opportunities), on a raw materials rather than a digital agenda.
developments:
[A signed memorandum establishes a critical raw materials strategic partnership](2023-10-26-eu-zambia-mou-sustainable-raw-materials-value-chains), the founding instrument of the relationship.

2025-11 — [more than EUR 200 million in Team Europe investments was announced at a corridor business forum, deepening the raw materials memorandum and the connectivity commitments](2025-11-12-commissioner-sikela-announces-team-europe-investments).

2026-02 — [a partnership dialogue was held at which the Union welcomed an invitation to deploy an election observation mission and reaffirmed corridor and raw materials cooperation](2026-02-26-team-europe-and-zambia-discuss-reforms-and-opportunities).

None of the three carries a digital or data component of its own. That is the finding: the largest external partnership on this ledger is minerals and corridors, and digital appears in it nowhere.

summary: A [co-operation agreement with a Qatari holding group](2025-08-21-idc-signs-co-operation-agreement-with-qatars-al-mansour) and a [joint business council with the Saudi chambers](2025-09-23-zambia-saudi-arabia-seal-business-council-deal), over a [US$1.1bn mining stake](2024-03-22-zccm-ih-transaction-completion-announcement-mopani-copper-mines).
developments:
[An investment of up to US$1.1 billion for 51 per cent of a copper mining company completed](2024-03-22-zccm-ih-transaction-completion-announcement-mopani-copper-mines) is the largest Gulf commitment in the country the base holds.

2025-08 — [the state industrial corporation signed a co-operation agreement with a Qatari holding group covering energy, agriculture, tourism, mining, transport and logistics, witnessed by the President](2025-08-21-idc-signs-co-operation-agreement-with-qatars-al-mansour).

2025-09-18 — [a chambers body and the Saudi chambers federation signed a memorandum establishing a joint business council](2025-09-23-zambia-saudi-arabia-seal-business-council-deal), an institutional channel distinct from the two deals.

Digital and data appear in none of them. The Gulf relationship here is mining and trade.

summary: A [comprehensive official bilateral brief](2026-04-01-india-zambia-bilateral-relations) lists memoranda and credit lines since 1964, with a [mutual legal assistance treaty in negotiation](2025-11-18-beyond-handshakes-zambia-india-mla-treaty).
developments:
2025-08-22 — [a framework agreement was signed for a pharmaceutical manufacturing joint venture, 51 to 49 per cent with the Zambian side](2025-08-24-akums-drugs-and-pharmaceuticals-manufacturing-plant-zambia).

2025-11-14 — [the prosecution authority and the Indian high commission held talks to finalise a mutual legal assistance treaty](2025-11-18-beyond-handshakes-zambia-india-mla-treaty) — a commitment being negotiated rather than concluded, and the one with the clearest data dimension, since mutual legal assistance is how evidence crosses a border.

2026-04 — [India's foreign ministry published a comprehensive bilateral brief listing memoranda, lines of credit, trade and investment since 1964](2026-04-01-india-zambia-bilateral-relations). It is the most complete external account of the relationship the base holds and it is the counterparty's own.
